name: Gambia
summary: Muslims are bound by Sharia inheritance rules under the Constitution, with a bequest limited to one third. Customary law governs other communities. Trusts and foundations were not sourced.
reserved_share: Among Muslims, Sharia fixed shares (Constitution; Cadi courts), with wasiyya (bequest) up to one third. Customary law applies to others and the Constitution exempts inheritance from non-discrimination rules.
foreign_law_note: No source on foreign law for non-Muslim resident foreigners.
trust_note: Trusts: no source found; 'yes' assumes English common-law trusts apply, which is unverified. No private-foundation law was found.
open_questions: A Wills Act is reported (1992) but not verified.
How a non-Muslim foreigner's will is treated not found.
Trust law and foundations not sourced.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
Domestic trusts: likely available under the inherited common-law or Roman-Dutch tradition, but no statute or official source was read; confirm before marking yes.
